{"reviewer":"R1-CORRECTNESS","lens":"correctness","verdict":"BLOCKED","findings":[{"id":"CRIT-001","severity":"CRIT","claim":"The forward-mode prior-green-CI safety check in enable-required-check.sh queries the GitHub check-runs API for the default-branch HEAD commit SHA. Because the adopter wrapper template (templates/adopter-wrapper.yml.tmpl) declares `on: pull_request:` only, its check runs are associated with PR head SHAs, not with the resulting merge commit on the default branch. For any adopter using merge-commit or squash-merge strategy, the default-branch HEAD commit will have zero `policy-check / scp/policy-check` check runs, so the query permanently returns empty. The safety check is non-functional: every invocation requires `--i-understand-this-repo-has-no-prior-green-ci`, completely defeating the foot-gun guard. The 60-day window specified in the DISPATCH-NOTE is also entirely absent from the implementation.","evidence":"enable-required-check.sh lines 248–257: `target_default_branch_sha=$(gh api repos/${REPO}/branches/${target_default_branch} --jq .commit.sha)` then `gh api repos/${REPO}/commits/${target_default_branch_sha}/check-runs --jq .check_runs[] | select(.name == policy-check / scp/policy-check) | select(.conclusion == success) | head -1`. GitHub Actions `pull_request:` check runs are keyed to the PR head SHA; a merge commit created by the merge-button has no descendant check runs from PR-triggered workflows. templates/adopter-wrapper.yml.tmpl line 6: `on: pull_request: branches: [{{DEFAULT_BRANCH}}]` — no `push:` trigger. DISPATCH-NOTE §5.4 spec: 'refuses forward-mode invocation against repo with no successful policy-check / scp/policy-check run on default branch in last 60 days'.","impact":"The safety check never fires as intended. Operators must always pass the bypass flag even after the adopter wrapper has accumulated dozens of green CI runs on PRs. The design goal of preventing enable-required-check.sh from running before the wrapper has green-CI'd is unachieved. Additionally, the missing 60-day filter means even a correct reimplementation that happened to find stale runs would not honour the freshness window.","mitigation":"Replace the per-commit check-runs query with a workflow-runs API call filtered by workflow name and a 60-day date window: resolve the workflow ID via `gh api repos/${REPO}/actions/workflows --jq .workflows[] | select(.name == policy-check) | .id`, then query `gh api repos/${REPO}/actions/runs?workflow_id=${wid}&status=success&created=>=$(date -u -v-60d +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)`. On systems without BSD date, use `python3 -c import datetime; print((datetime.datetime.utcnow()-datetime.timedelta(days=60)).strftime(...))`. If the paginated result is empty, refuse with the existing error message; if non-empty, proceed."},{"id":"MAJ-001","severity":"MAJ","claim":"The --restore mode log entry's 'Before' section shows restore_before_json (the original good state being restored TO), which is identical byte-for-byte to the 'PUT payload applied' section. The current degraded state before the restore is never captured. A forensic reader cannot determine from the log what the broken branch-protection configuration was that prompted the restore.","evidence":"enable-required-check.sh restore_branch_protection function: the PUT call at line 335 (`printf '%s' $restore_before_json | gh api -X PUT ... --input -`) is executed with no preceding GET to capture the current (degraded) state. Lines 362–371 of the heredoc emit both the 'PUT payload applied' block and the 'Before' block using `restore_before_json` — an identical variable reference. restore_after_json (line 339) captures the post-PUT state. The script header states: 'the audit trail records the SHA256 of the actually-running script content... the operator commits the resulting log entry whether the apply succeeded or partially failed, so the audit trail captures both outcomes' — the restore mode violates this by omitting the pre-restore state.","impact":"Post-incident forensic review cannot reconstruct what broken configuration prompted the restore. The 'Before' label is misleading: it documents the original good state (what we PUT) rather than the state we found. An operator reviewing the log for a security incident has no record of the intermediate degraded state. This violates the audit-trail contract that motivates every other log section.","mitigation":"Add `restore_current_state=$(gh api -X GET repos/${restore_repo}/branches/${restore_branch}/protection 2>/dev/null || echo {\"_note\":\"capture-failed\"})` immediately before the PUT call at line 335. In the heredoc, replace the 'Before' block expansion from `restore_before_json` to `restore_current_state`, and retitle 'PUT payload applied' to 'Restoring TO (original captured before-state)' so the log clearly distinguishes the target good-state from the observed bad-state."},{"id":"MIN-001","severity":"MIN","claim":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh anchors the onboarded-operator-bump STATUS.md regex with `(?m)^- \\*\\*` (bullet prefix) and `$` (end-of-line), contradicting the plan-doc §2 invariant 2 specification that the regex is file-agnostic. The blocked-on-adopter-conflict case correctly uses the non-anchored form, creating an asymmetric implementation across the two check-paths.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh line 193: `pattern = rf'(?m)^- \\*\\*TF-024X-renovate-{re.escape(slug)}(?:\\*\\*)? \\((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\\): \\S.{{19,}}$'`. Contrast with blocked-on-adopter-conflict at line 208: `pattern = rf'TF-024X-conflict-{re.escape(slug)}(?:\\*\\*)? \\((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\\): \\S.{{19,}}'` (non-anchored). Plan-doc §2 invariant 2: 'The regex is file-agnostic: it matches the TF reference content, not the surrounding markdown (so the same line passes whether it has a - **...** STATUS.md bullet wrapper, lives in a DISPATCH-NOTE prose paragraph, or is otherwise embedded)'.","impact":"Any STATUS.md TF entry for an onboarded-operator-bump adopter that is not in `- **TF-024X-renovate-{slug}** (status): desc` bullet format (e.g. in a table cell, inline prose, or a different list style) would fail CI even if fully compliant with the plan-doc spec. Current STATUS.md tracked-forward items always use bullet format, so there is no runtime impact for the current cohort. The asymmetry between the two check-paths is a latent contract drift risk for future STATUS.md reformatting.","mitigation":"Change line 193 to `pattern = rf'TF-024X-renovate-{re.escape(slug)}(?:\\*\\*)? \\((open|pending|in-progress|closed)\\): \\S.{{19,}}'` — matching the non-anchored blocked-on-adopter-conflict form and the plan-doc file-agnostic spec. Remove `(?m)^- \\*\\*` prefix and `$` suffix. The slug-specific anchoring is retained; only the surrounding-markdown anchors are dropped."},{"id":"MIN-002","severity":"MIN","claim":"The STATUS.md 024B table entry retains the literal placeholder `#<scaffolder-PR>` instead of the actual merged PR number, breaking the PR traceability chain that every preceding STATUS.md entry provides.","evidence":"STATUS.md line 142: `| 1 | #<scaffolder-PR> | **024B** | D-044 filed; protocol deviation noted; ...`. Every other STATUS.md table row references a concrete PR number (e.g. `#97`, `#98`, `#102`).","impact":"The audit trail from STATUS.md to the merged PR is broken. A reviewer following up on 024B governance cannot navigate from STATUS.md to the PR diff without searching commit history separately. Violates the STATUS.md convention established across all prior slices.","mitigation":"Replace `#<scaffolder-PR>` with the actual PR number at merge time, before the PR lands on main."},{"id":"nit-001","severity":"nit","claim":"The --restore mode invocation log entry includes `- **Required check:** policy-check / scp/policy-check` drawn from the REQUIRED_CONTEXT default. In restore mode, the operator never passes --required-check and the restore PUT applies the captured before-state verbatim regardless of REQUIRED_CONTEXT. The displayed value is the script default, not the state embedded in the before-state blob.","evidence":"enable-required-check.sh restore_branch_protection heredoc line ~364: `- **Required check:** \\`${REQUIRED_CONTEXT}\\``. In restore mode, REQUIRED_CONTEXT is initialised to `policy-check / scp/policy-check` (line 115) and never overridden because the argument-parsing guard prevents combining --restore with forward-mode flags (lines 186–190).","impact":"Minor forensic confusion: a reviewer reading the restore log entry may assume the restore specifically targeted the `policy-check / scp/policy-check` context when the actual restored required_status_checks are embedded in the before-state JSON block below.","mitigation":"Replace the 'Required check' line in the restore-mode heredoc with `- **MODE:** restore — required-check context derived from restored before-state (see PUT payload above)` to make the restore semantics unambiguous."},{"id":"nit-002","severity":"nit","claim":"DISPATCH-NOTE.md contains a duplicate `## Sequencing` section header on consecutive lines.","evidence":"DISPATCH-NOTE.md lines 130–131: `## Sequencing` appears twice in immediate succession before the sequencing table.","impact":"Cosmetic. No functional impact on any script, CI check, or reviewer decision. Renders as two identical headings in markdown.","mitigation":"Delete one of the two duplicate `## Sequencing` headers."}],"summary":"BLOCKED. One CRIT and one MAJ require fixes before 024C entry. CRIT-001: the forward-mode prior-green-CI safety check in enable-required-check.sh is non-functional — it queries check runs on the default-branch HEAD commit, which for any adopter using standard PR-triggered wrappers (pull_request: trigger only) will always return empty because GitHub associates those check runs with PR head SHAs, not merge commits. Every operator invocation is forced through the bypass flag, and the DISPATCH-NOTE-specified 60-day window is not implemented. MAJ-001: the --restore audit log omits the pre-restore degraded state; the Before section repeats the PUT payload, defeating the forensic purpose of the log. MIN-001 is a regex anchoring deviation (STATUS.md bullet-format assumption vs. plan-doc file-agnostic spec) with no current runtime impact. MIN-002 is a placeholder PR number that must be replaced before merge. nit-001 and nit-002 are cosmetic. All 13 worked-example test cases are present and correctly assert exit codes. ADOPT-001 §12.8 3-gate playbook, D-044 row shape, and STATUS.md section structure are all correct."}
